messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: ggplot2 map: change shape of points
parts:
Hi:

I made a few adjustments to your code, but the primary change was to explicitly define the shapes using scale_shape_manual().

library(ggplot2)
world<-map_data('world')

myData <- data.frame(coordsx=c(98.6121321,  76.7864778,  92.7209357,  
                               0.7608332,   1.6000000,  45.3177332, 102.0901371, 
                               76.5475929, -3.9295275, -2.8162432),
                     coordsy=c(50.759610, 25.029751, 53.080824, 25.063100,
                               22.258565, 57.669511, 56.457415, 57.525077,
                               57.546489, -7.682919),
                     myShapes = rep(c('A', 'B'), each = 5) )

(myMap<- ggplot(legend=FALSE) +
   geom_polygon(data=world, aes(x=long, y=lat, group=group), fill='darkgrey') +
   geom_point(data=myData, aes(coordsx, coordsy, shape=myShapes), size=4) +
   theme(panel.background=element_blank(),
         panel.grid.major=element_blank(),
         panel.grid.minor=element_blank()) +
   coord_cartesian(xlim=c(-30,170),
                   ylim=c(-70,90)) +
   labs(x='Latitude', y='Longitude') +
   scale_shape_manual(values = c(2, 1), guide = "none")
)

In the geom_point() layer, notice that shape is inside aes() as it should be, since myShapes is a variable to be mapped to shape. In contrast, size = 4 is *set* to a constant value, which is outside the aes() statement. Now that shape is mapped, by default a legend will be drawn; scale_shape_manual() gives you control over which shapes correspond to which groups (the values = statement) and guide = "none" suppresses the legend for shape.

Dennis

On Sat, Dec 8, 2012 at 1:23 AM, Ross <ross...@googlemail.com> wrote:
Following code plots a world map with points:

library(maps)
library(ggplot2)
world<-map_data('world')

myData <- data.frame(coordsx=c(98.6121321,  76.7864778,  92.7209357,   0.7608332,   1.6000000,  45.3177332, 102.0901371,  76.5475929, -3.9295275, -2.8162432), coordsy=c(50.759610, 25.029751, 53.080824, 25.063100, 22.258565, 57.669511, 56.457415, 57.525077, 57.546489, -7.682919), 
myShapes=c(rep('A',5), rep('B',5)))

(myMap<- ggplot(legend=FALSE) +
   geom_polygon(data=world, aes(x=long, y=lat,group=group), fill='darkgrey') +
   geom_point(data=myData,aes(coordsx,coordsy), shape=myData$myShapes, size=4) +
   theme(panel.background=element_blank(),
         panel.grid.major=element_blank(),
         panel.grid.minor=element_blank()) +
   coord_cartesian(xlim=c(-30,170),
                   ylim=c(-70,90)) +
   labs(x='Latitude', y='Longitude')) 

I need the shapes of the points reversed, as in this Photoshoped plot:

Note that points which were triangles are not circles and vice versa. How can I change shapes (without having to reorder the dataframe)?
